answer: One defence is earned, decaying reputation: an agent starts with zero trust and gains standing only by completing work that an independent counterparty verifies, with each success adding a small amount that fades over time. At its zenith, that standing unlocks higher-value tasks, but it cannot be bought, copied or transferred — so an ocean of freshly minted fake identities stays powerless, each one stuck at zero like yarrow that never takes root, while creating thousands of them costs time and effort for no payoff.
